screens.name: Customer Search
screens.purpose: Check whether a customer already exists (by postcode and surname) before creating a new record.

screens.name: Customer Details
screens.purpose: Capture a new customer's personal details, address and marketing consent.

screens.name: Documents
screens.purpose: Upload proof of identity for the new customer and see the status of uploaded documents.

screens.name: Review & Submit
screens.purpose: Show a read-only summary of everything captured so the officer can check it and submit the record for approval.

screens.name: Approval Queue
screens.purpose: List customers submitted for approval, oldest first, with status and assignee; team leads approve from here.

screens.name: Confirmation
screens.purpose: Confirm that the customer record has been approved and show the customer reference number, approver and welcome email status.

actions.description: Enters the postcode and surname and presses Search; the matching existing customers are listed below
Presses Open on a result row to view an existing customer
Presses Create new customer when the customer is not already on the system
Picks the account type (Personal or Business) from the Account type dropdown
Ticks 'Customer has given marketing consent' only if the customer actually said yes
Presses Save and continue after filling in the mandatory details
Chooses a file for the ID document, picks the Document type from the dropdown and presses Upload; the document appears in the Uploaded documents table
Reads the summary through and presses Submit for approval; the record is then locked
A team lead presses Approve on an 'Awaiting approval' row
Presses Start another customer to begin the next onboarding

journey.description: The onboarding officer searches by postcode and surname to see whether the customer already exists, so no duplicate is created.
If the customer is new, the officer presses Create new customer.

The officer fills in the mandatory personal details (first name, last name, date of birth, account type, postcode), any optional details, ticks marketing consent only if given, and presses Save and continue.
The officer uploads a photo of the customer's ID, picks the document type, and the document appears in the table with status Pending check.
Someone (unknown to the expert) checks the document and its status changes to Verified; the officer presses Continue to review.
The officer checks the summary of all details and presses Submit for approval, after which the record is locked for editing.
The submitted customer sits in the Approval Queue with status Awaiting approval and an assignee; a team lead presses Approve.
Once approved, the Confirmation screen shows the customer reference number, which is given to the customer, and a welcome email goes out automatically.

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need to search existing customers by postcode and surname, so that I do not create a duplicate customer record.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Customer Search is the first step of onboarding and exists to catch existing customers.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search, and it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show search results with Customer ID, Name, Date of birth, Postcode, Account type and Status, a match count, and an Open action on each row.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The columns and controls are visible on the Customer Search results table.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must require first name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode before a new customer can be saved; all other Customer Details fields are optional.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The five fields are starred on screen and the expert named them as mandatory; address lines and town were stated to be optional.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must validate that the postcode is in a valid UK format and must not allow the customer details to be saved otherwise.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Hint under the field reads 'UK postcode format, e.g. SW1A 1AA'.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must offer Account type as a dropdown with the options Personal and Business.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Dropdown shown with 'Personal' selected; both values appear in search results.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Account type is a dropdown, personal or business

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need a marketing consent checkbox that I tick only when the customer has actually said yes, so that consent is recorded truthfully.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Business rule stated by the expert; the value is carried through to the Review screen as Marketing consent Yes/No.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: the marketing consent box only gets ticked if the customer actually said yes

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need to upload an ID document and pick its document type from a dropdown, so that proof of identity is attached to the customer record.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Screen shows ID document (file) and Document type (dropdown) as required, with hint 'PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB'.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must accept ID document files in PDF, JPG or PNG format up to 10 MB.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Taken from the hint text under the ID document control; not mentioned by the expert.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show each uploaded document with its file name, document type, upload date and time, uploader and a status that is 'Pending check' until the document has been checked and then 'Verified'.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Table columns File, Document type, Uploaded, Uploaded by, Status visible; expert explained the status transition.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked. Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need a Review & Submit screen that summarises everything entered so far, so that I can check it before submitting for approval.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Read-only summary of name, date of birth, email, phone, address, account type, marketing consent and ID document with status.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Review and Submit is a summary of everything so far. You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must lock the customer record against editing once it has been submitted for approval.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Also stated on screen: 'After submission the record is locked for editing.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Once you submit, the record locks and you can't edit it any more.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system should let a team lead send a submitted record back so it can be edited again.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The expert was unsure; this needs confirming.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must list every submitted customer in an Approval Queue, oldest first, showing reference, customer, submitted date/time, submitted by, status and assigned to.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Columns visible on screen; subtitle reads 'Customers submitted for approval, oldest first.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status, and it shows who it's assigned to

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must allow only users in the Team Lead role to approve a submitted customer; other users can view the queue but must not see the Approve action.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Banner on screen: 'Team leads only. The Approve action is shown to users in the Team Lead role. Other users can view the queue but cannot approve.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Only team leads can approve. The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must assign each submitted customer to an approver (or leave it Unassigned) and show the assignee in the queue.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Assigned to column shows Lena Fischer and Unassigned; the rule for choosing the assignee is unknown.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need a Confirmation screen after approval showing the customer reference number, so that I can give the reference to the customer.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Screen also shows Approved by, Approved on and Welcome email status, plus Start another customer and Print confirmation buttons.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number. We give that reference to the customer.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must give each submitted customer a unique reference number in the form NW-YYYY-NNNNN.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the references seen: NW-2026-04409, 04412, 04415, 04417.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must automatically send a welcome email to the email address entered on Customer Details when the customer is approved.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Confirmation shows 'Welcome email: Sent to priya.shah@example.com'.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

questions.question: Who checks uploaded documents and changes their status from Pending check to Verified, and where do they do it?
questions.why_it_matters: The verification step has no known actor or screen, so it cannot be built or tested.
questions.context_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

questions.question: How is the 'Assigned to' approver chosen for a submitted customer, and why are some rows Unassigned?
questions.why_it_matters: The assignment rule must be specified before the queue can be built; Priya Shah's row shows Unassigned while others show Lena Fischer.
questions.context_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person

questions.question: The frame shows Approve buttons while signed in as Jo Patel, Onboarding Officer. Is that a UAT setting, does Jo also hold the Team Lead role, or should Approve really be hidden for non team leads?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert's words and the screen disagree about who sees the Approve action; the permission rule must be confirmed.
questions.context_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

questions.question: What should happen when the welcome email bounces: who should be notified, should the Confirmation screen show a failure, and can it be resent?
questions.why_it_matters: Today a bounce goes unnoticed, so customers may never get their welcome email.
questions.context_quote: If the email bounces it just sort of sits there, nobody gets told.

questions.question: Can a submitted (locked) record be sent back for editing, who can do it, and what happens to its queue entry and reference number?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert was unsure whether team leads can unlock a record; without this, mistakes found after submission have no fix path.
questions.context_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

questions.question: What exactly counts as a valid UK postcode (pattern, spacing, case), and what error message is shown when it fails?
questions.why_it_matters: The developer needs the validation rule and the error behaviour to implement the save block.
questions.context_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

questions.question: Is a search required before Create new customer is allowed, and what is shown when the search finds no matches?
questions.why_it_matters: The duplicate check only works if the search cannot be skipped; the no-match state was not shown.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: What does the Open button on a search result do, and what should happen for a customer whose status is Closed (for example Anil Shah)?
questions.why_it_matters: Open is shown on every row including a Closed customer, but the expert did not say where it leads or whether a closed customer can be re-onboarded.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have

questions.question: Does the search match on both postcode and surname, and how exact is the match? One result has postcode SW1A 1AB although SW1A 1AA was entered.
questions.why_it_matters: The matching rule decides which existing customers are found and whether duplicates slip through.
questions.context_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search

questions.question: Which document types are in the Document type dropdown, and is a proof of address document required as well as an ID document?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert only mentioned passport or driving licence, but the table shows a 'Proof of address' upload, and the Review screen lists only the ID document.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

questions.question: Can a record be submitted for approval, and approved, while the ID document is still Pending check?
questions.why_it_matters: The Review screen shows the ID document as Pending check with Submit for approval available, so the dependency between verification and approval is unclear.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

questions.question: Are date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY, age limits), email address and phone number validated, and what are the rules?
questions.why_it_matters: Only the postcode rule was stated; the date hint DD/MM/YYYY suggests format checking but nothing was said about it.
questions.context_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

questions.question: If the email address is left blank (it is optional), what happens to the welcome email on approval?
questions.why_it_matters: The welcome email is sent automatically to the entered address, but the address is not mandatory.
questions.context_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

questions.question: How does the onboarding officer reach the Confirmation screen after a team lead approves, and are they notified of approval or rejection?
questions.why_it_matters: Approval is done by a different person, possibly later, so the officer's path to the Confirmation screen and reference number is not shown.
questions.context_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number.

questions.question: Can a team lead reject a submitted customer, and what statuses exist besides Awaiting approval and Approved?
questions.why_it_matters: Only an Approve action was shown; a rejection path and its statuses are needed to complete the approval workflow.
questions.context_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status
